scope: New SignedDiscreteCopy + DiscreteCorrect modules, shared SignedCopy macro and original Python/source comparison
result: No defect found in explicitly stated logical single-program discrete-copy contract; original-program scope remains incomplete.

findings.finding: All 9 discrete profiles instantiate the same kcacheSignedSource% macro used by signed floating source; the macro retains all token/sequence/head/split coordinates and metadata reads. Statement-count theorem is explicitly only a sanity check.

Signed widths 8/16/32/64 map BitVec.toInt, unsigned widths map toNat, boolean maps BitVec 1 nonzero. payloadValue_injective preserves every finite representation, including negative signed values, high-bit unsigned values and both bool values.

loaded and copied are independent specifications over initial memory. Data has no arithmetic or cast; proof executes complete source and matches initial-load/fold-store effect. outputOffset is injective in lane index, yielding readback and full frame.

Whole source performs metadata reads and data tile load before destination writes, and copied uses the initial state for all those reads. Single-program source/output aliasing is therefore preserved by the proved effect.

Logical .int/.nat tags erase machine storage widths; finite payload injection recovers the source value domain, but storage ABI and byte representation remain explicitly separate. This is not a native memory layout theorem.

remaining_original_scope: Python reshape branch k.dim()==4, n>1 batch branch and both use_new_kcache_layout branches are not covered by these new modules.
3D host grid (bsz*n,heads,head_dim//x), num_warps branch, source stride wiring and global launch coverage/disjointness remain unproved.

Signed logical metadata and Nat offsets do not establish native fixed-width runtime arithmetic, pointer conversions, negative-offset behavior or ABI. The native integer-address refinement is structural and cannot be deferred as a numerical assumption.
